summary: Ezekiel uses עָגַב for desiring lovers and עֲגָבִים for the passion they arouse (Ezk 23:5, 16–17). Genesis pairs the instrument עוּגָב with the lyre (Gen 4:21). Its connection with the words for desire is uncertain.

senses.definition: To desire someone passionately as a lover.

evidence.note: On seeing the Chaldeans depicted on the wall, she desires them and sends messengers to them.

senses.definition: A musical instrument, probably a pipe.

evidence.note: The עוּגָב and the lyre are both objects of תֹּפֵשׂ, describing the instruments Jubal’s successors handle.
People rejoice at the sound of the עוּגָב in a scene of music with tambourine and lyre.
The עוּגָב is named alongside strings among the instruments of praise.

senses.definition: The passion of lovers, also the subject of a love song.

evidence.note: The Babylonians come to her bed of love.
The listeners enjoy hearing the prophet as they would a well-sung love song.
